reading.body:
All six podcasts here publish transcripts or detailed show notes, making them searchable primary sources rather than audio-only commentary.

The set spans distinct registers: scout-report capability analysis, long-form researcher interviews, engineering-depth technical coverage, and practitioner-accessible explainers. A reader choosing one is not choosing between quality levels but between audiences and framings. The oldest entry covers a decade of machine learning practice, which gives it archival value that newer shows cannot yet match.

The data does not cover episode counts, publication frequency, or audience size, so no ranking by influence or reach is possible from it. Nothing here connects directly to compute, infrastructure, or power, the binding constraints this site centers. These podcasts are knowledge infrastructure, not physical infrastructure, and the data says nothing about whether their coverage of hardware and grid constraints is substantial or thin.
